newsitem.title: USA: Northern States nuke seen down into March.
newsitem.headline: Northern States nuke seen down into March.

text.p: Northern States Power Co's 500 megawatt (MW) Prairie Island nuclear power unit 2 is expected to be out of service until early March for scheduled refueling and maintenance, a company spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The unit, in Red Wing, Minn., was shut Jan 24 and is expected to be down for about 40 days, said spokeswoman Mary Heimstead.
"It is a basic refueling outage, the unit has to be taken down about every 18 months," Heimstead said, adding restart was expected to occur near March 5.
Northern States has made arrangements to purchase power on the spot market to replace that lost by the outage, the spokeswoman said.
"We will make up the difference through routine purchases and through increased generation from our other units," she said.

Northern States also operates the 503 MW Prairie Island 1 nuclear power unit, which continues to operate normally at full power, and the 544 MW Monticello nuclear plant in Monticello, Minn., which also continued to operate normally.
